title: DP II: Grid DP & Interval DP (Depth Pass)
relevance: High — post-Striver second wave: CF/AtCoder/CSES packings of path grids, 2×n tilings/columns, and dp[l][r] merges that OAs still reuse under contest wrappers.
company_notes: 2-row / strip games: pick from two rows of heights without consecutive same-row → Basketball Exercise (common OA recoloring of path DP). Min operations to unify a segment: recolor connected same-value components / paint fence with horizontal or vertical strokes → Flood Fill / Painting Fence interview variants. Seat assignment / taxi pickup on a line: move people to empty seats minimizing total |Δ| → Armchairs (sequence DP disguised as matching). Edit / align two strings: Edit Distance table remains the OA default for grid-shaped DP interviews (contest form CSES, not LeetCode).

phases.goal: Confirm the candidate sees the same grid/interval engines under contest wrappers—2×n strips, run compression, sparse obstacles, or length-ordered [l,r] merges.

must_hit.point: Same engines as the base topic—dp[r][c] on grids and length-ordered dp[l][r] on arrays/strings—but statements hide the template: 2-row / column / tiling states, lex-min frontiers, sparse obstacle path counts via binomials, flood-fill / bracket / fence recursions, matching people↔positions, or compress-runs-then-interval-DP.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names grid dp[r][c] / interval dp[l][r] and lists several hide-the-template skins (2×n, sparse binomials, flood-fill/fence, ordered matching, run compression).

must_hit.point: Recognize it when moves stay right/down (or along a 2×n strip), when only contiguous segments matter, or when cost/ways on [l,r] depend only on strictly smaller intervals.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States right/down or 2×n strip, contiguous segments, or [l,r] depending on smaller intervals as the membership test.

must_hit.point: OA skins: 2-row strip pick without consecutive same-row (Basketball Exercise); unify/recolor a segment or paint fence horizontal vs vertical (Flood Fill / Painting Fence); seat people into empty chairs minimizing Σ|Δ| (Armchairs); Edit Distance as the default grid-shaped OA DP.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps the prompt to one of those four Where-it-appears skins.

probes: What makes this depth-pass grid/interval DP rather than a plain path-sum or MCM template?
If the statement hides a 2×n strip, run recolor, fence strokes, sparse walls, or line seating, what family do you reach for?

hints.1: Ask whether the template is disguised even though the engine is still dp[r][c] or length-ordered dp[l][r].
hints.2: Cue: right/down or 2×n strip; contiguous segments; [l,r] cost/ways from strictly smaller intervals; skins include tiling/column states, run compression, sparse binomials, fence/bracket, ordered matching.
hints.3: Say: same dp[r][c] / dp[l][r] engines; recognize on right/down, 2×n, contiguous [l,r]; OA maps are Basketball Exercise, Flood Fill / Painting Fence, Armchairs, Edit Distance.

phases.goal: Pick the right rewrite—run compression, horizontal/vertical fence branch, sparse binomial obstacle DAG, ordered line matching, or lex-min frontier—before coding.

must_hit.point: Flood Fill: first compress equal-color runs; then dp[l][r] = min recolors to make the run-segment monochrome; matching endpoints often let you absorb a side cheaper than painting from scratch.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States RLE then interval DP on runs, plus absorb-via-matching-endpoints.

must_hit.point: Painting Fence: recurse on unfinished [L,R] above height h—either pay (R−L+1) vertical strokes, or paint one horizontal layer and split into contiguous unpainted subsegments (horizontal vs vertical branch, not MCM-for-k).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes vertical pay-(R−L+1) vs horizontal layer then split; rejects MCM-for-k framing.

must_hit.point: Sparse Grid 2: with huge H,W and few walls, paths((r1,c1)→(r2,c2)) = C(Δr+Δc, Δr); sort walls; dp[i] = ways to first hit wall i (subtract paths that hit an earlier wall)—inclusion on the obstacle DAG.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Quotes binomial path counts plus DP only on sorted obstacles with earlier-wall subtraction.

must_hit.point: Armchairs / ordered matching: people and empty chairs on a line—dp[i][j] = cost placing first i people into first j chairs (chair j unused, or person i sits there); monotone sequence DP, not bipartite matching flow.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States people×chairs prefix DP and rejects flow/bipartite matching.

must_hit.point: Minimal Grid Path: at manhattan step t, keep only cells still compatible with the lexicographically best prefix so far; take the min letter among candidates, discard the rest—frontier shrinks, no O(n²) string DP.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes per-diagonal compatible frontier and min-letter pick without storing full path strings.

probes: Before coding, is this run-interval recolor, fence horizontal/vertical, sparse binomial obstacles, ordered seating, or a lex-min frontier?
For Flood Fill vs Painting Fence vs Grid 2 vs Armchairs vs Minimal Grid Path, which rewrite do you pick?

hints.1: Classify RLE-interval vs fence branch vs binomial-obstacle DAG vs line matching vs lex frontier.
hints.2: Flood Fill compresses runs then absorbs matching ends; Fence pays vertical (R−L+1) or splits after a horizontal layer; Sparse Grid uses C(Δr+Δc, Δr) and DP on walls; Armchairs is dp[i][j] on prefixes; Minimal Grid Path shrinks a compatible frontier.
hints.3: Say: RLE then dp[l][r] with absorb; vertical vs horizontal-layer split; binomials + first-hit wall DP; people×chairs sequence DP not flow; keep only still-optimal cells per step t.

phases.goal: Verify length-ordered interval loops, 2×n last-column states, factorial/binomial setup for sparse grids, and canonical outer structure for brackets/fences.

must_hit.point: Write length-ordered interval loops (len, then l, set r=l+len-1) and know when to add a split k vs only endpoint transitions.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States len→l→r=l+len-1 ordering and distinguishes split-k from endpoint-only transitions.

must_hit.point: Compress equal runs before Flood-Fill-style interval DP; never interval-DP the raw n=5000 array without RLE when runs dominate.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Insists on RLE before interval DP when n=5000 and runs dominate.

must_hit.point: 2×n / column DPs: state is configuration of the last column (colors, fused/separate, group count)—not a full H×W table.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names last-column configuration (fused/separate, colors, groups) instead of full grid DP.

must_hit.point: Sparse large grids: precompute factorial/invfactorial; path counts are binomials; DP only on the obstacle list. Empty String: when pairing s[i] with equal s[k], empty [i+1,k−1] then [k+1,j], multiply by binomials that interleave the two emptying sequences.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions fact/invfact + obstacle-only DP and/or pair-then-binomial-interleave for emptying.

must_hit.point: Bracket/fence recursions: identify the canonical outer structure (matching pair / height layer) before writing transitions. Coloring Brackets: only matching pairs get colors; state is interval plus colors of the outer pair.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names matching-pair or height-layer as the outer structure, and outer-pair colors for brackets.

probes: How do you loop intervals by length, and when is RLE mandatory before Flood Fill?
Sketch last-column state for a 2×n DP versus factorial/binomial setup for sparse Grid 2.

hints.1: Think len-ordered fills, run compression, and last-column vs obstacle-list state.
hints.2: Loops: len, l, r=l+len-1; RLE before interval DP at n=5000; 2×n keeps last-column config; sparse grids use fact/invfact and DP on walls; brackets/fences start from matching pair / height layer.
hints.3: Say: length-ordered (len,l,r); never raw n=5000 without RLE; last-column not H×W; binomials + obstacle DP; Empty String multiplies interleaving binomials; color only matching outer pairs.

phases.goal: State when O(n³) interval DP is OK, when n≤5000 forces O(n²) after compression or endpoint-only transitions, and what 2×n / ordered-matching costs look like.

must_hit.point: Always check n≤400/500 ⇒ O(n³) interval OK; n≤5000 ⇒ need O(n²) after compression or endpoint-only transitions.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Quotes n≤400/500 for O(n³) and n≤5000 needing O(n²) via compression or endpoint-only.

must_hit.point: Ordered matching on a line (Armchairs): one pointer for people, one for seats—O(#people · #chairs). Counting Towers: 2×n tiling DP with fused vs separate top cells; precompute to 1e6.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites O(#people · #chairs) and precompute-to-1e6 for towers.

must_hit.point: Lex-min / multi-criteria grid paths: advance a frontier of still-optimal cells; don’t store full path strings in DP (avoids O(n²) string DP). Sparse grids DP only on the obstacle list, not the full H×W table.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates frontier shrink from full-string DP, and obstacle-list DP from full grid.

probes: What n bounds make O(n³) interval DP safe versus forcing O(n²) after compression?
What complexity do you quote for Armchairs, Counting Towers precompute, and lex-min frontier vs string DP?

hints.1: Separate the n≤400/500 vs n≤5000 fit check from people×chairs and frontier costs.
hints.2: n≤400/500 → O(n³) OK; n≤5000 → O(n²) after RLE or endpoint-only; Armchairs O(#people · #chairs); towers precompute to 1e6; lex-min keeps a frontier, not O(n²) strings.
hints.3: Say: n≤400/500 ⇒ O(n³); n≤5000 ⇒ O(n²) via compression/endpoints; Armchairs O(#people · #chairs); Counting Towers to 1e6; frontier not full path strings; sparse DP on obstacles only.

phases.goal: Catch missing RLE, full H×W on strips, flow for line seating, full path strings for lex-min, and MCM framing of fence/bracket recursions.

must_hit.point: Interval-DP on the raw n=5000 array without RLE when runs dominate (Flood Fill needs compress equal-color runs first).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Corrects to RLE then dp[l][r] on runs for Flood Fill.

must_hit.point: Treating 2×n / column problems as a full H×W table instead of last-column configuration (colors, fused/separate, group count).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Insists on last-column state for 2×n / column DPs.

must_hit.point: Casting Armchairs as bipartite matching flow instead of monotone sequence DP dp[i][j] on first i people and first j chairs.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects flow; states people×chairs ordered DP.

must_hit.point: Painting Fence as MCM-for-k, or storing full path strings for Minimal Grid Path / skipping the compatible frontier; Sparse Grid walking the full grid instead of binomials + obstacle DAG.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names horizontal/vertical fence branch, frontier not strings, and binomials+obstacles not full-grid walk.

probes: What goes wrong if you skip RLE on Flood Fill, build H×W for a 2×n strip, or run flow on Armchairs?
How do fence horizontal/vertical branching, lex-min frontiers, and sparse binomial DP save you?

hints.1: Check run compression, last-column state, and whether seating is sequence DP.
hints.2: Flood Fill needs RLE at n=5000; 2×n is last-column not H×W; Armchairs is dp[i][j] not flow; Fence is horizontal vs vertical not MCM-for-k; lex-min keeps a frontier; Sparse Grid uses binomials on walls.
hints.3: List: compress runs first; last-column config; people×chairs sequence DP; fence pay (R−L+1) or split after a layer; frontier of still-optimal cells; C(Δr+Δc, Δr) + first-hit obstacle DP.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: On unfinished [L,R] above height h, either pay (R−L+1) vertical strokes or paint one horizontal layer and split into contiguous unpainted subsegments—classic horizontal vs vertical branch, not MCM-for-k.

tradeoffs.topic: Absorb matching endpoints vs paint from scratch (Flood Fill)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: After compressing equal-color runs, matching endpoints often let you absorb a side cheaper than painting from scratch; start-square choice folds into which run you grow from.

tradeoffs.topic: Sequence DP vs bipartite matching flow (Armchairs)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: People and empty chairs on a line use dp[i][j] = cost placing first i people into first j chairs (chair unused or person sits there)—monotone structure, not bipartite matching flow.

tradeoffs.topic: Lex-min frontier vs O(n²) string DP (Minimal Grid Path)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: At manhattan step t keep only cells compatible with the lexicographically best prefix so far, pick the min letter, discard the rest—frontier shrinks; do not store full path strings in DP.

tradeoffs.topic: Binomials on obstacle DAG vs full grid DP (Sparse Grid 2)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: With huge H,W and few walls, path counts are C(Δr+Δc, Δr); sort walls and DP ways to first hit each wall (subtract earlier-wall paths)—inclusion on the obstacle DAG, not a full H×W table.

tradeoffs.topic: 2×n last-column state vs full H×W table
tradeoffs.strong_answer: For 2×n / column DPs the state is configuration of the last column (colors, fused/separate, group count), not a full H×W table.

gotchas.trap: Interval-DP the raw n=5000 array without RLE when runs dominate (Flood Fill).
gotchas.correction: Compress equal-color runs first; then dp[l][r] = min recolors to make the run-segment monochrome.

gotchas.trap: Building a full H×W DP for 2×n / column / tiling problems.
gotchas.correction: State is configuration of the last column (colors, fused/separate, group count).

gotchas.trap: Treating Armchairs as bipartite matching / flow.
gotchas.correction: Use ordered matching DP: dp[i][j] cost of first i people into first j chairs in O(#people · #chairs).

gotchas.trap: Framing Painting Fence as MCM-for-k splits.
gotchas.correction: Recurse on unfinished [L,R] above height h: pay (R−L+1) vertical strokes, or paint one horizontal layer and split into contiguous unpainted subsegments.

gotchas.trap: Storing full path strings for lex-min grid paths.
gotchas.correction: Maintain a frontier of cells still compatible with the best prefix; take the min letter each step and discard the rest.

gotchas.trap: Walking the full grid for sparse obstacle path counts.
gotchas.correction: Precompute factorial/invfactorial; paths = C(Δr+Δc, Δr); DP only on the sorted obstacle list with earlier-wall subtraction.

gotchas.trap: Using O(n³) interval DP at n≤5000 without compression or endpoint-only transitions.
gotchas.correction: n≤400/500 ⇒ O(n³) OK; n≤5000 ⇒ need O(n²) after compression or endpoint-only transitions.
